title: Lesson 3 - Grounding Generative AI: Einstein Trust Layer, Retrieval Augmented Generation, and Unstructured Data
description: Articulate Data 360's foundational role in generative and predictive AI, covering how Data 360 grounds generative AI through the Einstein Trust Layer and retrieval augmented generation over structured and unstructured data.

questions.question: Which Einstein Trust Layer capability ensures that a third-party large language model provider neither trains on nor retains your prompts and data?
questions.explanation: Zero data retention is the Trust Layer guarantee that no data is used for training and nothing is retained by the third-party model. Prompt defense limits harmful or injected outputs but does not govern retention, which is the strongest distractor's mistake.

questions.question: A team wants an AI agent to answer questions from internal PDFs and support transcripts. Through which Data 360 capability are those documents made retrievable at prompt time?
options: Retrieval augmented generation over a vector database
questions.explanation: Unstructured files are chunked, vectorized into a vector database, and retrieved to ground prompts, which is retrieval augmented generation. Calculated insights compute metrics from structured data and do not index documents.

questions.question: Which statement about Data 360 grounding for generative AI is correct?
options: Only structured data can ground a prompt
Grounding requires copying all data into the model
Grounding ignores user permissions because the model runs outside Salesforce
Secure data retrieval merges grounding data while preserving the running user's permissions and field-level security
questions.explanation: Dynamic grounding with secure data retrieval honors the running user's permissions and field-level security. The first option is the classic wrong belief, and the Trust Layer is built specifically to preserve those controls.
